answer: Because the velvet forfeiture is applied at exit, the crystal ledger totals each burn, and the atlas audit records the amount lost per key. Exiting before the lock expires forfeits 46% of the bond outright, and the forfeit is burned and therefore nobody profits from it. An operator that moves capital between 20 aliases therefore destroys value on every move, which makes rotation strictly worse than leaving the bond in place. That is 19 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
